messages:
Ava: digging through a Perfetto trace for a customer repro — end-to-end latency spike on small chat requests. Client->gateway looks fine, but runtime token generation jumps ~300ms for some requests. link: https://perfetto.link/trace/abcd :thinking:
Liam: can you paste the trace id + a short snip of the timeline? is the spike correlated with a kernel launch or memcpy?
Ava: trace id is abcd. Screenshot of flame + timeline attached in thread (see perfetto). Key spans: client->gateway (30ms), gateway->runtime RPC (~10ms), runtime total ~350ms for the slow one. Runtime spans show a long wait labeled "kv_cache_miss:populate" then a sequence of kernels.
Rachel: interesting — did you check batching heuristics? if the request hit an off-batch path it might force a slow full-kernel path. Any pattern on request length?
Ava: these are tiny prompts (<=64 tokens). Most requests are 40–60ms. The slow ones are also small tokens but show repeated small kernel launches.
Sam: @Ava can you dump the nsight/nsys timeline for the same run? perfetto is great for spans but kernel-level hotspots need nsys to see cuLaunchKernel timings and occupancy.
Ava: uploaded an nsys capture as well. On nsys the slow trace shows many kernel submissions with low occupancy and a long gap between them. nvprof indicates several tens of microseconds per kernel + queueing.
Liam: that smells like kernel selection mismatch. New kernel selector picks a specialized small-token kernel that actually has higher overhead for tiny batches due to register spilling. Did you try forcing the generic kernel?
Ava: forced generic kernel via env KERNEL_SEL=generic and re-ran. Slow path dropped from 350ms to ~80ms. Perfetto trace now shows one heavy kernel instead of many small ones.
Rachel: ok that's a good signal. Also KV cache behavior: if kvcache populate is synchronous it can block the incoming request. Is the populate path running on main runtime thread or a background worker?
Ava: current code path populates synchronously when miss and kvcache size < threshold. There's an async debounce in the pipeline but not for cold misses.
Sam: propose short-term mitigation: 1) make kv cache populate async for client-facing requests, 2) revert kernel selector default for tiny sequences while we tune heuristics, 3) add Perfetto trace events around kvcache ops.
Liam: agree. Also add a perf regression test: synthetic load where seq_len=32 and batch=1, capture nsys + perfetto automatically. If median > 2× baseline fail.
perfbot: automated trace capture uploaded: https://perfetto.link/trace/abcd, nsys bundle: s3://redwood-nsys/1719823456-abc.tgz
Ava: repro steps I used:
```
# run on dev-runtime-3
export KERNEL_SEL=auto
export KV_ASYNC=0
./runtime_server --model t5-small --port 8080 &
python tools/loadgen.py --rate 50 --seq-len 32 --batch 1 --capture-perfetto /tmp/trace.pb
```
Ava: next actions: I will: (a) flip kvcache populate to async behind a config flag, (b) add a kernel selector override flag and run the synthetic perf job, (c) add perfetto markers for kvcache start/end. Will post follow-ups here.
Rachel: also add a tiny unit in the model onboarding flow so kernel profiles for seq<=64 are recorded at upload time. That can guide selector heuristics.
Liam: once you have the async flag and selector toggle, I can run a canary on dedicated cluster and capture perfetto + nsys to validate.
Ava: thanks — ETA EOD for the async flag patch. Will attach updated traces. :thumbsup:
Sam: nice investigation thread. If you want I can add an alert rule around median kernel count per request so we catch regressions automatically.
Ava: yes please, that'd help. I'll link the perf tests PR when ready.
